blocks.heading: Evidence Coverage and Bounded Use
blocks.text: The registered bibliographic inventory establishes the empirical and computational baseline for this theoretical proposal. MESA binary-evolution infrastructure supplies the differential-rotation and implicit mass-transfer machinery needed to model accretion-driven angular momentum redistribution, while its explicit exclusion of common-envelope and contact-binary phases marks the current computational boundary of the recycling pathway. Population-synthesis evidence confirms that binary interaction through tides, mass transfer, and mergers shapes rotation-rate distributions, yet the same literature identifies mass-transfer efficiency and magnetic braking as the dominant sources of uncertainty in derived outcomes. Dense-matter constraints from GW170817 and joint microscopic–macroscopic analyses anchor the causal speed-of-sound bound that the relaxed equilibrium axioms must preserve; the radius inference in particular is conditional on whether the equation of state is required to support masses above 1.97 solar masses. NANOGrav narrowband and wideband timing campaigns, together with the Fermi gamma-ray pulsar catalog, define the millisecond-pulsar population and magnetospheric context against which any proposed mass–spin relation must be tested. These sources ground the proposal's premises without supplying evidence for the candidate mechanism itself.

blocks.heading: Unknown-Item Consequences
blocks.text: Two canonically assigned records gate the completion of this design. The degraded counterexample-analyzer stage produced no retained formalization, counterexample, or protocol detail, so no conclusion about counterexamples may be drawn from the current evidence chain; qualified human review must replace the discarded batch before the design is treated as complete. Independently, the mechanism_mass_spin_relation is referenced throughout the formal spine as the derived function M = R(P), yet its specific functional form remains undefined, which blocks any numerical verification of the mass–spin prediction and leaves the associated derivation steps unverified. These are not generic caveats: each is a precise procedural dependency that must be resolved upstream before the candidate theorem's proof obligations can be discharged.

blocks.heading: Transition to the Next Stage
blocks.text: The evidence inventory is therefore complete in its bounded role: it supplies the computational, microphysical, and observational premises on which the proposal stands, and it delineates the release criteria that future claims must satisfy. What it does not supply is the missing counterexample analysis and the closed-form mass–spin relation, both of which are assigned to human review. The next stage inherits these constraints directly: any candidate lemma, derivation chain, or falsifier matrix must operate within the registered evidence boundary, treat the undefined relation as an open formal dependency rather than an established result, and defer theorem-status updates until the assigned review items are resolved.
